Diagnosis.submission: The faulty component is the audit-log-archiver CronJob (and its accumulating Job pods) in namespace hotel-reservation. Root cause: its pod template pairs a one-shot archiver container that exits 0 (Completed) with a fluent-bit-sidecar container that runs forever (nc -lk -p 24224). Because the sidecar never terminates, every Job pod stays NotReady forever and the Job never reaches Succeeded. With schedule * * * * * and concurrencyPolicy Allow, plus no ttlSecondsAfterFinished or activeDeadlineSeconds, a new job/pod is spawned every minute and left behind (16+ permanently NotReady pods and growing), so the critical KubePodNotReady alert (pod has been not ready for more than 1 minute) fires continuously for all of them - these are the only active critical alerts in the namespace. The reservation application itself is healthy: frontend, search, geo, rate, profile, recommendation, reservation, user and the mongodb/memcached backends all respond, and I verified end-to-end /hotels, /recommendations with require=dis/rate/price, /user login and a successful /reservation; there are no DB authorization errors and mongodb-geo/mongodb-rate admin users retain their readWrite roles. Secondary anomaly: Services jaeger, jaeger-agent, jaeger-collector and jaeger-query select labels that match no pods and expose no ports, so they have no endpoints and no traces are collected for the namespace (only jaeger-out has endpoints and reports 0 traces).

Diagnosis.submission: The frontend-proxy Deployment in namespace astronomy-shop was tampered with (revision 2, annotations edge.platform/change-ticket=EDGE-1847, edge.platform/filter-profile=managed-rules-v2): the standard Envoy edge-proxy container was replaced by a single-threaded Perl script acting as a naive WAF, with command /usr/bin/perl -e and env WAF_RULE_REGEX=^([a-zA-Z]+)*$. This regex contains nested quantifiers and is vulnerable to catastrophic backtracking (ReDoS). Any request carrying a waf= query parameter with a long value (production logs show candidateLength=5001) makes the single-threaded proxy burn ~1-3 seconds of CPU per request (verified in-container: a 5000-char non-matching candidate blocks ~3s), stalling ALL edge traffic; page loads through the proxy take ~0.9s versus ~0.00s when hitting the frontend directly. Additionally, when a waf parameter is present the Perl script short-circuits and returns 200 "ok" without forwarding to the frontend (traffic hijack), and it dropped the original Envoy routing (e.g., /jaeger now 404s). Root cause: unauthorized/misconfigured replacement of the edge proxy introducing a ReDoS-prone regex in a single-threaded WAF. Fix: revert frontend-proxy to the original Envoy-based pod spec (remove the Perl command/args, WAF_* env vars, and EDGE-1847 annotations).

Diagnosis.submission: Root cause: an injected deny-all NetworkPolicy named deny-all-recommendation in namespace hotel-reservation isolates the recommendation service. The policy selects pods with label io.kompose.service=recommendation and declares policyTypes Ingress+Egress with no allow rules, so all ingress/egress traffic to/from the recommendation pod is dropped (including its MongoDB dependency mongodb-recommendation:27017). Evidence: (1) blackbox probe recommendation.hotel-reservation:8085 has probe_success=0 with the critical alert ServiceEndpointDown firing, while frontend, geo, profile, rate, reservation, search and user probes all return 1; (2) probe connections to recommendation:8085 hang until the 5s timeout (DNS lookup succeeds, TCP connect is blackholed); (3) a direct connection attempt from another pod to recommendation:8085 times out, whereas search:8082 responds normally; (4) the recommendation pod itself is Running/Ready with 0 restarts and clean logs, and even its request to the DB fails because the policy also blocks egress; (5) the ingress probe for /api/hotels (a recommendation-dependent frontend route) also fails. Faulty component: recommendation service, blocked by NetworkPolicy deny-all-recommendation. The fix is to remove the blocking policy to restore connectivity.

Diagnosis.submission: The frontend-proxy (Envoy) Deployment in namespace astronomy-shop has been tampered with: a duplicate environment variable FRONTEND_HOST=localhost was appended to the container spec (the Deployment is at revision 2 while all other deployments are revision 1). The original FRONTEND_HOST=frontend is overridden by the later duplicate, so the running pod has FRONTEND_HOST=localhost. Envoy renders its config via envsubst, and the frontend upstream cluster is defined as ${FRONTEND_HOST}:${FRONTEND_PORT}, so the proxy now routes all incoming requests (/) to localhost:8080 (itself) instead of the frontend Service, resulting in HTTP 503 Service Unavailable from the application entry point. Evidence: requests to http://frontend-proxy:8080/ return 503 while http://frontend:8080/ returns 200; frontend pod logs show ECONNREFUSED to product-catalog only during startup; all flagd fault-injection flags are off. Root cause: misconfigured FRONTEND_HOST=localhost env var in the frontend-proxy deployment.

Diagnosis.submission: Root cause: the nginx-thrift frontend pod crashloops with OOMKilled because a mutating admission webhook (registered as kyverno-resource-mutating-webhook-cfg, served by the platform-policy-controller Deployment in the platform-ops namespace) rewrites the memory requests/limits of container[0] of every pod created in the social-network namespace to a hardcoded 16Mi, overriding the Deployment manifest values (128Mi request / 256Mi limit). The openresty-based nginx-thrift container cannot run within 16Mi, so it is instantly OOMKilled (exit 137) and enters CrashLoopBackOff; as the frontend/entry point, this makes the entire application unreachable. Evidence: deployment/nginx-thrift spec has memory limit 256Mi, but the created pod nginx-thrift-6bb8c75d64-tckz4 has limits/requests memory=16Mi; lastState shows OOMKilled exitCode 137; the webhook server code in ConfigMap platform-policy-controller-server (platform-ops) hardcodes MEMORY="16Mi" and patches /spec/containers/0/resources/(requests|limits)/memory on pod CREATE. Faulty component: platform-policy-controller webhook (platform-ops) clobbering pod resources; victim: nginx-thrift / social-network frontend.

Diagnosis.submission: The cleanup-controller in namespace hotel-reservation is unable to remove the finalizer from the ConfigMap reservation-cleanup-token, leaving it stuck in Terminating state. Root cause: an RBAC misconfiguration — the ClusterRole configmap-cleanup-controller (bound to ServiceAccount cleanup-controller via ClusterRoleBinding configmap-cleanup-controller) only grants verbs get/list/watch on configmaps and is missing the patch/update verb. Diagnosis.submission: Root cause: the Kafka orders pipeline in namespace astronomy-shop is deadlocked on a poison-pill record. The custom consumer deployment 'orders-validator' (running configmap orders-pipeline-scripts/consumer.py, consuming topic orders-fulfillment) hit a truncated/malformed JSON message at topic offset 20 -- the record reads {"order_id":"ORD-100020","amount": (invalid JSON, build error 'Expecting value: line 1 column 35'). The consumer's error handling deliberately pauses the partition forever (infinite 1s sleep loop) and never skips or commits past the bad offset, so consumption halts permanently at offset 20. Evidence: orders-validator logs repeat 'record validation failed at offset=20' / 'partition remains paused at offset=20'; the downstream topic orders-processed stopped at exactly 20 records while orders-fulfillment kept growing (160+ messages); the orders-validator consumer group sat at offset 20 with lag continuously increasing (36 -> 78+). Faulty components: the orders-validator consumer (non-resilient poison-message handling) and the malformed message in the orders-fulfillment topic produced by the order-stream/seed data. Secondary observations: product-catalog restarted twice at startup (exit code 1) causing brief connection-refused errors seen in frontend/recommendation logs, but it is now serving normally; kafka pod was OOMKilled once (exit 137) and restarted, losing its ephemeral /tmp topic data.

Diagnosis.submission: GET /api/recommendations through frontend-proxy hangs for 15s and returns HTTP 504, while all other endpoints work. Root cause: the recommendation Service is misconfigured with internalTrafficPolicy: Local (injected at 12:57:17Z by a non-Helm manager OpenAPI-Generator), and injected nodeSelectors pin the recommendation pod to node kind-worker and the frontend deployment to node kind-worker2 (both also injected at 12:57:17Z and followed by rollout restarts). With Local traffic policy, the recommendation ClusterIP only routes to pods on the client pod node, so cross-node calls from the frontend (kind-worker2) to recommendation (kind-worker) are blackholed and time out. Evidence: from a kind-worker2 pod, connecting to the recommendation ClusterIP times out while the pod IP connects instantly; from a kind-worker pod, the ClusterIP connects instantly; recommendation is the only application Service with internalTrafficPolicy: Local. Faulty components: recommendation Service (Local traffic policy) and the frontend/recommendation Deployments (injected nodeSelector pins). Fix direction: restore Cluster traffic policy on the recommendation service and remove the injected nodeSelectors.

Diagnosis.submission: Faulty component: CoreDNS configuration in kube-system namespace (the coredns ConfigMap Corefile). An injected rule was added to the Corefile: "template ANY ANY user-service.social-network.svc.cluster.local { match ^user-service.social-network.svc.cluster.local\.$ rcode NXDOMAIN fallthrough }". This makes CoreDNS return NXDOMAIN for user-service.social-network.svc.cluster.local, so no pod in the cluster can resolve the user-service hostname (verified: resolution fails from nginx-thrift and social-graph-service pods for both short and FQDN names, while compose-post-service, social-graph-service, post-storage-service, unique-id-service etc. all resolve fine). Impact: all RPCs that need to find user-service fail with "Could not resolve host for client socket" - nginx-thrift logs show repeated ComposePost failures (compost_post failure) on POST /wrk2-api/post/compose, breaking social network functionality that depends on user-service lookup. Root cause: the broken CoreDNS template rule (service-discovery sabotage) in the coredns ConfigMap; removing the rule and reloading CoreDNS restores resolution.
